alignments.note: Rule 40: the subordinating negative conjunction is realized by the word introducing the English clause; no negative indefinite follows, so rule 59 does not empty it.
Rules 17 and 66: 'man' is a generic completion of the indefinite, so the head stays on 'any'.
Rule 9: auxiliary rides with the lexical verb, which is the head.

Rules 7 and 36: the ASV expands the preposition into the complex 'in the matter of', so the supplied nominal frame rides with 'in', headed on the word that realizes the preposition. Giving 'the matter of' to the article instead remains defensible.

Rule 38: the attributive demonstrative 'this' occupies the determiner slot of 'bounty', so the article governing that expressed head noun realizes nothing; rule 38 states that rule 22 is not the contrast where a head noun is expressed.
Rules 23 and 31: second attributive article governing an expressed head noun; the relativizer and copula are the participle's helpers.
Rule 31: attributive participle rendered as a finite clause takes 'which is' as helpers.
